whyEn: This chapter is where the exam checks whether you can keep yourself alive and functional for a 30-year career: the physiology of stress (the alarm reaction, the sympathetic cascade, and the slide from chronic stress into exhaustion), what a critical incident does to a crew and what CISM offers afterward, how burnout builds, and the concrete armour of the job — standard precautions, the immunization list, postexposure steps, lifting mechanics with real numbers, fatigue and shift-work rules, and the grim statistics on line-of-duty deaths and ambulance crashes. Questions from here are unusually factual for a 'wellness' topic: stage names, hour counts, distances, and sequences, not feelings.
whyZh: 这一章考的是：你能否让自己在这行健康地干满三十年。压力的生理机制（警报反应、交感级联、慢性压力滑向耗竭的全过程）、批判事件对班组的冲击与事后的 CISM、职业倦怠如何积累，以及这份工作的硬防具——标准预防、免疫接种清单、暴露后流程、带真实数字的举升力学、疲劳与轮班规则，再加上殉职与救护车事故那几组冷冰冰的统计。别看主题叫『身心健康』，出题却异常硬核：考的是分期名称、小时数、距离和流程顺序，不是感受。

sections.titleEn: Introduction: What the Old Culture Cost

points.en: The chapter opens with the cautionary tale of a veteran wrecked by the old culture: 'the patient always comes first' as a slogan, 24-hour shifts every third day, fast food gulped after the last late-night call, cigarettes between runs — and stretchers lifted from the side by two paramedics, hands about 45 cm apart between spread knees, a technique that quietly ground down knees, hips, and backs. Thirty years of research later, the point of the chapter is that none of those injuries were inevitable.
points.zh: 本章以一位被旧文化耗垮的老救护员开场：口号是『患者永远第一』，每三天一个24小时班，深夜最后一单跑完才狼吞虎咽快餐，出勤间隙抽烟——担架靠两人从侧面抬，双膝叉开、双手间距约45厘米，这套动作年复一年地磨损膝、髋和腰背。三十年研究走过来，本章要说的正是：那些伤病本来一样都不必发生。

points.en: Your obligation is double: ensure your own well-being, and pass what you learn to other professionals and the public. A partner's burnout is not private either — the case study asks outright whether a cranky partner's attitude affects prehospital patient care, and the chapter's answer is yes.
points.zh: 你的义务是双份的：既要守住自己的身心健康，也要把学到的传给同行与公众。搭档的倦怠也不是他的私事——案例开门见山地问：搭档的坏态度会不会影响院前救护？本章的答案是：会。

sections.titleEn: Components of Well-Being: Body, Mind, Emotion, Spirit
sections.titleZh: 身心健康的组成：身体、心理、情绪与精神

points.en: Wellness is an active set of processes and choices — not an absence of illness — and it is multidimensional: physical, mental, and emotional at minimum, with many adding a fourth essential dimension, the spiritual. Exam answer: three named dimensions plus a widely endorsed fourth.
points.zh: Wellness 是一组主动的过程与选择——不是『没生病』——而且是多维的：至少包括身体、心理、情绪三个维度，许多人认为还有不可或缺的第四维——精神/灵性。考试答案：三个列名维度＋一个广被认可的第四维。

points.en: Canada's Food Guide (2019) in plate form: nearly half fruits and vegetables, one quarter protein foods from animal or plant sources, one quarter whole grains — and water as the first-choice beverage. Following it meets vitamin and mineral needs and cuts the risk of obesity, type 2 diabetes, heart disease, certain cancers, and osteoporosis. Calorie anchor: a sedentary man aged 19 to 30 needs 2,500 calories a day; active, 3,000.
points.zh: 《加拿大膳食指南》（2019）的餐盘公式：将近一半是蔬菜水果，四分之一是蛋白质食物（动物或植物来源均可），四分之一是全谷物——饮品首选水。照做能满足维生素矿物质需求，并降低肥胖、2型糖尿病、心脏病、某些癌症和骨质疏松的风险。热量锚点：19–30岁久坐男性每天2,500千卡；活跃者3,000千卡。

points.en: The paramedic eating strategy: plan meals before reporting for duty, carry bottled water and minimize caffeine, and keep numerous small snacks — raisins, nuts, fruit — so you eat when hungry instead of speed-eating big, expensive, high-fat meals after the last late call.
points.zh: 救护员的进食策略：上班前就计划好餐食；随身带瓶装水、少喝咖啡因；备足小份零食——葡萄干、坚果、水果——饿了就吃，而不是拖到深夜最后一单之后狼吞虎咽又贵又高脂的大餐。

points.en: Activity math worth memorizing: Canada's Physical Activity Guide calls for 30 to 60 minutes of moderate activity built into daily life, accumulable in bouts of at least 10 minutes; for cardiovascular endurance, adults need at least 30 minutes of moderate to vigorous activity most days of the week. Exercise should target three areas — cardiovascular endurance, flexibility, and strength.
points.zh: 值得背下的运动数字：《加拿大身体活动指南》要求每天累计30到60分钟中等强度活动，可拆成每次至少10分钟的小段；要练出心血管耐力，成人每周大多数天都要有至少30分钟中到高强度活动。训练应瞄准三块：心血管耐力、柔韧性、力量。

points.en: Target heart rate is a four-step calculation: measure resting heart rate; subtract your age from 220 for estimated maximum; take (maximum minus resting) × 0.7; add resting back. Worked example: 40 years old, resting 70 — maximum 180, difference 110, × 0.7 = 77, target 147 beats/min. The shorthand the book states: target is 70% of maximum — but never overexert to injury.
points.zh: 目标心率是四步算术：测静息心率；用220减年龄得估算最大心率；（最大−静息）×0.7；再加回静息心率。算例：40岁、静息70——最大180，差值110，×0.7＝77，目标147次/分。书中给的速记：目标为最大心率的70%——但绝不要练到过度或受伤。

points.en: Circadian rhythms are governed by the suprachiasmatic nuclei — the brain's internal clock. Fighting them costs sleep, higher thought, physical coordination, even social function. The shift-work survival trio: avoid caffeine, eat healthy meals at the same times daily, keep a regular sleep schedule. And the hard limit: a paramedic awake and working 18 to 20 hours straight cannot keep driving an emergency vehicle or administering medications without sleep.
points.zh: 昼夜节律由『视交叉上核』掌管——大脑的内置时钟。硬扛节律的代价是睡眠、高级思维、肢体协调乃至社交功能全线受损。轮班生存三件套：避开咖啡因、健康三餐定点吃、睡眠时间表固定。还有一条硬上限：连续清醒工作18到20小时的救护员，不睡觉就不能再开急救车、不能再给药。

points.en: Periodic health risk assessments start from heredity: Alzheimer disease, chemical addiction, cancer, cardiac illness, hypertension, migraine, mental illness, and stroke all carry prominent hereditary factors — and the two most common hereditary risks are heart disease and cancer. Share the family history with your physician, who is bound by the same confidentiality oath you are, and build screening into routine checkups.
points.zh: 周期性健康风险评估从家族遗传入手：阿尔茨海默病、物质成瘾、癌症、心脏病、高血压、偏头痛、精神疾病、卒中都有显著遗传因素——其中最常见的两项遗传风险是心脏病和癌症。把家族史告诉你的医生（他和你受同一份保密誓言约束），把筛查排进常规体检。

points.en: Body mechanics doctrine, point by point: minimize the number of total-body lifts (keep the stretcher at hands height, never fully lowered, so you bend only once); coordinate every lift in advance with the team AND the patient — a patient panicking mid-lift and grabbing a neck throws everyone off balance; minimize the weight (extra lifter at the foot end, strip unneeded equipment); never carry what can roll — ambulance and stretcher as close as possible, stair chair if needed; and ask for help without embarrassment.
points.zh: 举升力学信条，逐条数：减少全身抬举的总次数（担架预置在手高位、绝不完全放到底，这样只需弯腰一次）；每次抬举都提前协调——团队要知道分工，患者也要知道流程，否则患者半空慌了抱住谁的脖子，全组失去平衡；减少要抬的重量（脚端加一人、卸掉不必要的设备）；能滚的绝不扛——救护车和担架尽量贴近患者，必要时用楼梯椅；开口求助不丢人。

points.en: The back rule has no exceptions: the human back is a great weight bearer but a terrible lifter. Keep the back straight and upright, lift without twisting, feet about shoulder-width with your centre of gravity balanced, lower your upper body by bending the legs, then lift by straightening them. Legs lift; the back only carries.
points.zh: 护腰规则没有例外：人的腰背是优秀的承重者、糟糕的举重者。背部挺直、抬举时不扭转，双脚约与肩同宽、重心站稳，弯的是腿而不是腰，起身靠双腿蹬直完成。腿负责举，背只负责承。

points.en: Fight-or-flight is a physiologic package triggered by profound stress — increased sympathetic tone: pupils dilate, heart rate climbs, bronchi dilate, glucose mobilizes, blood shunts away from the GI tract toward cerebrum and skeletal muscle — all inside 20 seconds. The exam-worthy cost list: clumsy speech, lost depth perception and visual acuity, masked pain, and lost fine motor control exactly when you need manual dexterity. Mild stress, by contrast, sharpens mental acuity.
points.zh: 『战或逃』是深度应激触发的整套生理反应——交感张力上升：瞳孔散大、心率加快、支气管扩张、葡萄糖动员、血液从胃肠道转向大脑与骨骼肌——全程不到20秒完成。考点在代价清单：说话变笨拙、深度知觉和视敏度下降、痛觉被掩盖、恰恰在最需要手上精细活时丢掉精细运动控制。对照记：轻度压力反而让头脑更敏锐。

points.en: Emotional survival rules the book actually states: EMS should never be a paramedic's whole life — 'don't love something that can't love you back'; patients can die regardless of how good their paramedics, nurses, or trauma surgeons are, and patient death is not your fault unless you let your skills, education, or professionalism decay. Practical tools: let patients' misfortunes remind you of your own luck, keep a scrapbook of thank-you notes, cultivate non-EMS relationships — and speak up when a colleague stops taking care of themselves.
points.zh: 教材白纸黑字的情绪生存法则：EMS 绝不该是救护员的全部人生——『别爱一个不会爱你的东西』；无论救护员、护士、创伤外科医生多优秀，患者都可能死亡，而患者的死不是你的错——除非你放任自己的技能、学识或职业素养荒废。实用工具：让患者的不幸提醒你自己的幸运；把每张感谢卡都存进剪贴簿；经营 EMS 圈外的人际关系——发现同事不再照顾自己时，要开口说出你的担心。

points.en: Spiritual well-being for the working paramedic reduces to one professional obligation: whatever your own views, recognize that patients' spirituality may differ, respond respectfully to its expressions, and understand that respect for patients' beliefs directly helps you deliver effective prehospital care.
points.zh: 对执业救护员而言，精神维度落到一条职业义务上：无论你自己信什么，都要承认患者的灵性观可能与你不同，对其表达报以尊重——而对患者信仰的尊重，会直接帮助你完成有效的院前救护。

sections.titleZh: 压力：生理机制、患者反应与职业倦怠

points.en: Hans Selye, the father of stress theory, defined biological stress as the nonspecific response of the body to any demand made upon it — nonspecific because the same physiologic cascade fires whatever the threat. A stressor is any agent or situation requiring adaptation. His two categories: eustress, the positive stress that drives achievement, and distress, the overwhelming, debilitating kind — the only kind the rest of the chapter means by 'stress'.
points.zh: 『压力理论之父』Hans Selye 给生物学压力下的定义：机体对加诸其上的任何需求的非特异性反应——『非特异』是因为无论威胁是什么，点燃的都是同一套生理级联。stressor（应激源）＝任何需要人去适应的因素或情境。他分出两类：eustress（正性压力，推动人成就事业）与 distress（负性压力，压垮人、削弱人）——本章后文说的『压力』专指后者。

points.en: Triggers that stress the vast majority of people, per the book's list: loss of a loved one or valued possession (death, divorce), personal injury or illness, major life events (starting or finishing school, marriage, pregnancy, children leaving home), and job-related stress (conflict, excessive responsibility, threat of job loss or change). Coping starts with a personal inventory of your own triggers.
points.zh: 教材列出的『绝大多数人都会中招』的应激源：失去挚爱的人或珍视之物（丧亲、离婚）；自身伤病；重大人生事件（入学毕业、结婚、怀孕、子女离家）；职业压力（人际冲突、责任过重、可能失业或换岗）。应对的第一步是盘点你自己的应激源清单。

points.en: The acute stress sequence: the alarm reaction fires within a fraction of a second of a strong stimulus, opening with the alert response — you stop everything and lock onto the source, like a startled deer freezing mid-graze. Sympathetic stimulation follows: constricted blood vessels, increased heart rate, dilated pupils, erect hair follicles, perspiration. In animals, fight or flight dissipates the stress, relaxation follows, and balance returns. The modern problem: a death or a lost job offers no fight-or-flight outlet, so the body sits in continuous unrelieved alert — chronic stress — ending in exhaustion and ill health.
points.zh: 急性应激的顺序：强刺激出现后不到一秒，警报反应（alarm reaction）启动，开场是警觉反应——你停下一切、锁定刺激源，就像受惊的鹿骤然定住。随后交感神经全面点火：血管收缩、心率上升、瞳孔散大、毛发竖立、出汗。动物靠『战或逃』把压力泄掉，继而放松、回到平衡。现代困境在于：亲人离世、工作丢了，既没得打也没处逃，身体只能持续挂在无处释放的警戒态上——这就是慢性压力——终点是耗竭与疾病。

points.en: The stress response itself is normal — and misreading the body's fight-or-flight preparations as signs of disease only stacks anxiety on top. Your own early warning signs: heart palpitations, rapid breathing, chest tightness, sweating — plus behavioural tells like breathlessness, unnecessary shouting, and cursing you would not normally use.
points.zh: 应激反应本身是正常的——把身体为『战或逃』做的准备误读成疾病征兆，只会给焦虑再加码。你自己的早期预警信号：心悸、呼吸急促、胸口发紧、出汗——外加行为端倪：喘不上气、无端吼人、爆出平时不会说的粗话。

points.en: Three named on-the-spot management techniques, in the book's order: controlled breathing (deep breaths in through the nose, out through the mouth — the least obvious way to steady yourself on a call); reframing (replace 'I can't do this' with 'I trust my training, I can do this'); progressive relaxation (after the call, tighten then release specific muscle groups until the whole body lets go).
points.zh: 三种点名的现场自控技术，按书中顺序：控制呼吸（鼻吸口呼的深呼吸——出勤时最不露痕迹的镇定法）；重构（把『我做不到』换成『我相信我的训练，我做得到』）；渐进性放松（收队后逐组绷紧再放松肌肉，直到全身松弛）。

points.en: The lifestyle rules come with time windows: avoid excessive caffeine; avoid alcohol during the 24 hours before a duty day; exercise vigorously and regularly, especially during the 12 hours preceding a shift; get enough rest; keep laughter and compatible partners in the mix. Scepticism is valuable — cynicism is not: limit time in environments and with people who no longer care about EMS.
points.zh: 生活方式规则带着明确时间窗：咖啡因别过量；值班日前24小时不碰酒精；规律进行高强度锻炼，尤其在上班前12小时内；保证休息；让笑声和合拍的搭档常在。审慎怀疑是美德——愤世嫉俗不是：少泡在不在乎 EMS 的环境里，少和犬儒的人长期搭班。

points.en: Patients move from awareness of unpleasant sensations to anxiety, then once they accept illness, five common reactions follow: fear (of pain, disability, death, or their economic effects), diffuse anxiety (rooted in helplessness and lost control — worst in people whose self-esteem rides on being active and independent), depression (the natural response to loss of function and control), anger (born of fear and discomfort, vented on you as the nearest target — never truly aimed at the rescue team), and confusion (commonest in older patients; counter it by explaining who you are at the outset and keeping a running commentary).
points.zh: 患者的心理轨迹：先察觉不适、继而焦虑，接受患病现实后出现五种常见反应——恐惧（怕疼、怕残、怕死，或怕经济后果）；弥漫性焦虑（源于无助与失控——自尊建立在独立强干之上的人最易中招）；抑郁（对失去功能与掌控的自然反应）；愤怒（由恐惧和不适孕育，冲你发泄只因你离得最近——从不是真冲着救援队来的）；意识混乱（老年患者最常见；对策是开场就说明你是谁、来做什么，并持续口头讲解你的操作）。

points.en: Four defence mechanisms, all automatic and subconscious: denial — symptoms minimized with 'only' and 'a little' ('it's only a little indigestion'), countered by finding a reliable informant among family or friends; regression — retreat to an earlier age level, the toilet-trained 10-year-old who starts bedwetting after stress; projection — attributing one's own unacceptable feelings to others; displacement — redirecting an emotion from its true cause (the cardiac problem) onto a nearer substitute (the paramedic). Displacement explains most patient anger at crews; the professional accepts it without complaint.
points.zh: 四种心理防御机制，全是自动的、潜意识的：否认——用『只是』『一点点』淡化症状（『只是有点消化不良』），破解法是从家属朋友中找可靠的知情人；退行——退回更早的年龄段，比如早已学会如厕的10岁孩子在应激后重新尿床；投射——把自己不可接受的感受安到别人头上；转移——把情绪从真正的源头（心脏问题）改道泼向更近的替身（救护员）。患者冲班组发火多半是转移在起作用；专业的做法是照单收下、不抱怨。

points.en: Culture shapes stress display: some cultures read open emotion as weakness — absence of visible distress is not absence of distress, so read body language; lowered eyes may signal deference to your uniform, not evasion; many patients want no physical contact before rapport, so obtain permission before hands-on encounters. The frame to memorize: reactions are different, not wrong or abnormal. Family and bystanders run the same machinery — guilty parents of an injured child convert guilt into aggression at you via projection and displacement; your unbroken calm is the tool that improves everyone's behaviour, including your own.
points.zh: 文化决定压力怎么表现：有的文化视外露情绪为软弱——看不见痛苦不等于没有痛苦，要去读肢体语言；垂下眼睛可能是对你制服的敬意，不是回避；许多患者在建立信任前不愿被触碰，动手前先取得允许。要背的框架句：那些反应只是不同，不是错误或异常。家属和旁观者跑的是同一套机制——孩子被撞的父母把内疚经投射和转移换算成对你的攻击性；而你雷打不动的镇定，正是改善现场所有人（包括你自己）行为的工具。

points.en: Multiple-casualty reactions — the American Psychiatric Association's five categories, each with its disposal: anxiety (sweating, trembling, weakness, nausea, vomiting — recovers within minutes; give the shaky crew member a specific task); blind panic (judgment gone entirely — contagious, can ignite mass panic; separate the person fast, supervised by someone calm); depression (numbed, dazed — bring back to reality, remove from scene); overreaction (compulsive talking, inappropriate joking, racing uselessly between tasks — remove from the treatment area); conversion hysteria (anxiety converted subconsciously into bodily dysfunction — sudden blindness, deafness, or limb paralysis). General rule: people showing these reactions should be removed from the scene.
points.zh: 群体伤亡事件中的反应——美国精神病学会的五类，各配处置法：焦虑（出汗、颤抖、无力、恶心甚至呕吐——几分钟内可恢复；见队友发抖就派个具体任务：『去把这条静脉通路开起来』）；盲目恐慌（判断力全失——会传染、可点燃集体恐慌；立即隔离，交给冷静者看管）；抑郁（麻木呆滞——拉回现实、带离现场）；过度反应（说个不停、不合时宜地开玩笑、忙来忙去一事无成——请出救治区）；转换性癔症（焦虑被潜意识转换成躯体功能障碍——突然失明、失聪或肢体瘫痪）。总原则：出现这五类反应的人都该带离现场。

points.en: People define their own emergencies: the woman who called 9-1-1 because she could not sleep was facing her first night alone after her husband's funeral — such callers are not abusing the system; they are precisely who EMS exists for. The paired warning: tunnel vision about 'nonemergency' complaints causes assessment mistakes and worse outcomes, because seemingly minor complaints sometimes are not minor at all.
points.zh: 紧急与否由患者自己定义：那位因『睡不着』拨打911的女士，正熬着丈夫葬礼后独自过的第一夜——这样的呼叫者不是在滥用系统，他们恰恰是 EMS 存在的意义。配套警告：对『非紧急』主诉的隧道视野会导致评估失误和更差的结局——看似鸡毛蒜皮的主诉，有时一点也不小。

points.en: Burnout is the exhaustion of physical or emotional strength — a consequence of chronic, unrelieved stress, but crucially it develops from HOW a person reacts to stress: distress is a learned reaction rooted in beliefs. The five false perfectionist beliefs the book lists: I must be perfect all the time; my safety depends on anticipating every danger; I am totally responsible for what happens to patients — if they die it is wholly my fault; if there is something I don't know, people will think less of me; a good paramedic never makes mistakes. Prevention begins with recognizing all five as unrealistic and invalid.
points.zh: 职业倦怠＝体力或情感力量的耗竭——是慢性、未获缓解的压力的后果，但关键在于：倦怠取决于人**如何回应**压力——distress 是一种习得的反应，根子在信念。教材列出的五条错误的完美主义信念：我必须永远完美；我的安全取决于能预判每一种危险；患者的一切后果全由我负责——他们死了就全是我的错；要是有我不懂的东西，别人会看轻我；好救护员从不犯错。预防从承认这五条全部不现实、不成立开始。

points.en: Impending-burnout symptom screen: chronic fatigue and irritability; cynical negative attitudes; no desire to report to work; emotional instability (easy crying, hair-trigger temper, inappropriate laughter); changed sleep with unrefreshing waking; feeling overwhelmed, helpless, or hopeless; lost interest in hobbies; falling concentration; declining health — frequent colds, stomach upsets, headaches and backaches; constant muscle tightness; overeating, smoking, or abusing drugs or alcohol. The paramedics who last 20 years without burnout share one secret: they learned to respect and value themselves — altruists who still meet their own needs.
points.zh: 倦怠先兆自查表：慢性疲劳与易怒；犬儒式消极态度；不想去上班；情绪不稳（动辄流泪、一点就炸、不合时宜地大笑）；睡眠模式改变且醒来不解乏；被压垮感、无助感、无望感；对爱好失去兴趣；专注力下滑；健康走低——总感冒、总闹胃、头痛背痛不断；肌肉持续紧绷；暴食、抽烟或滥用药物酒精。干满20年不倦怠的救护员共守一个秘诀：学会尊重和珍视自己——利他者也照顾自己的需要。

points.en: Nancy's burnout-prevention guidelines, the testable specifics: aerobic exercise at least 30 minutes, three to four times a week; no self-abuse (smoking, alcohol overindulgence, recreational drugs, self-prescribing); daily 'me' time, with meditation named as a tool of the most stress-resistant paramedics; hobbies and social life outside EMS; leave the job behind after shift; drop the demand to be perfect or always right — a mistake now and then does not end the world; stay in touch with feelings, find someone to talk to, cry when needed; shed stress on duty rather than letting it accumulate, and debrief after tough calls.
points.zh: Nancy 的防倦怠守则，可考的具体项：有氧运动每次至少30分钟、每周三到四次；不自我伤害（吸烟、酗酒、消遣性用药、自行开药）；每天留出『自己的时间』，冥想被点名为抗压能力最强的救护员的工具；在 EMS 之外经营爱好与社交；下班就把工作放下；放弃『必须完美、必须永远正确』——偶尔犯错天不会塌；与自己的感受保持联结、找得到可以倾诉的人、想哭就哭；压力当班就释放、不留着累积，艰难出勤后要复盘（debrief）。

points.en: Kübler-Ross's five stages of grieving, in order with each stage's function: denial buffers the bad news until resources can be mobilized; anger replaces denial when reality can no longer be ignored — 'Why me?', displaced randomly onto whoever is near; bargaining tries to cut a deal that postpones the inevitable ('let me live to see my daughter's wedding'); depression arrives when bargaining fails — an enormous sense of loss; acceptance sees the dying disengage, shedding fears and loosening ties to the living.
points.zh: Kübler-Ross 的哀伤五阶段，按顺序连同各阶段的功能记：否认——缓冲噩耗，为调集心理资源争取时间；愤怒——现实再也否认不掉时取代否认，『为什么是我？』，火气随机泼向身边任何人；讨价还价——试图做笔交易推迟不可避免之事（『让我活到女儿婚礼，我就安心走』）；抑郁——交易失败后袭来的巨大失落；接受——临终者开始与世界脱钩，卸下恐惧、松开与生者的纽带。

points.en: Two stage-specific traps: in depression, do not try to cheer the person up — they want permission to express sorrow in words, tears, or what Kübler-Ross calls the silence that goes beyond words; offer tissues, offer the hug if wanted, accommodate the wish to be alone, and steer their behaviour only if it is harmful. In acceptance, the person needing the most help is usually the family, not the patient.
points.zh: 两个阶段专属陷阱：抑郁期不要去『哄开心』——对方要的是获准表达悲伤，用语言、眼泪，或 Kübler-Ross 所说的『超越言语的沉默』；递纸巾、想要拥抱就给、想独处就配合，只有行为有害时才去干预。接受期里，最需要帮助的通常是家属，而不是患者本人。

points.en: With a dying patient, the most important thing you can do is signal that talking about death is allowed — not by asking 'do you want to talk about dying?' but with 'if there's anything worrying you, I'd be glad to listen'; then actually listen, and make unmistakable physical contact, a held hand or a hand on the shoulder. To 'Am I going to die?', acknowledge the seriousness without stripping all hope: 'You seem to have had a severe heart attack. We're going to give you the best care available, but the situation is serious.'
points.zh: 面对临终患者，你能做的最重要的事是发出『可以谈死亡』的信号——不是直接问『想聊聊死亡吗』，而是说『有什么让您担心的，我很愿意听』；然后真的听，并给出不容误解的身体接触——握住手，或一只手搭在肩上。被问『我会死吗？』时，承认严重性但不抽走全部希望：『您看起来心脏病发作得很重。我们会给您最好的救治，但情况确实严重。』

points.en: Field wisdom the exam can quote: people who know they are dying usually do not ask — they look you in the eye and tell you. Preserve the dying patient's control and dignity: explain what you are doing, let them participate in treatment, ask whether there is anyone to contact — and if they give you a message to convey, write it down word-for-word as they state it.
points.zh: 可以直接进考题的现场经验：知道自己将死的人通常不问——他们直视你的眼睛，直接告诉你。要守住临终者的掌控感与尊严：解释你在做什么、让其参与治疗、询问是否需要联系什么人——若对方托你传话，要一字一句照原话记下来。

points.en: The grieving-family checklist runs against instinct: do NOT hide the body from the family even if badly mutilated (hide it from the general public) — families blocked from seeing the body can be trapped in denial and struggle to grieve; do NOT use euphemisms like 'expired' or 'passed away' — the family needs to hear the word 'dead'; do NOT rush to pack the resuscitation equipment — seeing it tells them everything possible was tried; give time with the remains, moving them into the ambulance for privacy if death occurred in public; recruit a neighbour or offer to call clergy; and accept guilt, shock, denial, or anger — their anger is not really at you.
points.zh: 安抚丧亲家属的清单条条反直觉：不要把遗体藏起来不让家属看——哪怕毁损严重（对公众才要遮挡）——被拦着见不到遗体的家属可能困在否认里、迟迟走不出哀伤；不要用『走了』『去世了』之类的委婉语——家属需要听到『死亡』这个词；不要急着收拾复苏设备——让家属看见它们，等于告诉他们能做的都做了；给家属与遗体相处的时间，若死在公共场所就把遗体移入救护车、让家属在车里独处告别；找位邻居来陪，或提出帮忙联系神职人员；接纳内疚、震惊、否认或愤怒——那愤怒并非真的冲你。

points.en: Grieving children by age band: up to 3 years — aware something happened and people are sad; keep the routine, watch irritability, eating, and sleeping. 3 to 6 — believe death is temporary, may keep asking when the person returns, may feel responsible and fear everyone else they love will die too; stress that they were not responsible and that crying is OK. 6 to 9 — may mask feelings to avoid looking babyish; discuss normal grieving and let them see adults cry. 9 to 12 — may want the details; encourage sharing feelings and memories.
points.zh: 儿童哀伤按年龄段分层：3岁以下——知道出事了、大家在难过；维持生活规律，观察易怒、进食和睡眠。3–6岁——以为死亡是暂时的，可能反复问『他什么时候回来』，可能觉得是自己害的，还会担心所爱的人都会死；要反复强调不是他的错、想哭就哭。6–9岁——可能掩饰情绪以免显得幼稚；和孩子谈哀伤的正常感受，大人也不必避讳当着孩子流泪。9–12岁——可能想知道事件细节；鼓励分享感受与回忆。

points.en: A critical incident is defined as one that overwhelms the ability of a paramedic or an EMS system to cope, at the scene or later. The trigger list for debriefing: serious line-of-duty injury or death of a fellow worker, suicide of a fellow worker, multiple-casualty incidents, serious injury or death of a child, and intense media attention. Reactions are unpredictable person to person — so debriefing is offered, never forced.
points.zh: 批判事件（critical incident）的定义：超出救护员个人或整个 EMS 系统应对能力的事件——无论当场压垮还是事后发作。需要考虑安排复盘的事件清单：同事因公重伤或殉职、同事自杀、群体伤亡事件、儿童重伤或死亡、媒体高强度聚焦。每个人的反应无法预测——所以复盘只能提供，绝不强制。

points.en: The CISM numbers and the honest caveat: a defusing session runs about 30 minutes right after the call, aiming to strip the explosive potential before it detonates later; a formal CISD is coordinated by professional counsellors 24 to 72 hours after the incident, lasts about 3 hours, away from the workplace and confidential. Purpose: accelerate normal recovery and affirm that these are normal people having normal reactions to abnormal events. The controversy the book states outright: after more than 20 years of use, there is no evidence CISDs are effective — nor evidence that their effects are not harmful.
points.zh: CISM 的数字与教材直言的保留意见：defusing（情绪疏泄会）约30分钟、紧接出勤之后进行，目的是在『炸药』引爆前拆除引信；正式 CISD 由专业辅导员在事发后24到72小时内组织，历时约3小时，地点远离工作场所、全程保密。宗旨：加速正常恢复过程，并确认参与者是『正常人对异常事件做出的正常反应』。教材毫不讳言的争议：用了20多年，却没有证据表明 CISD 有效——也没有证据表明它无害。

points.en: PTSD is the condition CISDs were built to prevent: an especially traumatic call preoccupying even a well-adjusted provider for weeks or months. Report to superiors if you notice the sign list: cannot get the incident out of your thoughts, flashbacks, nightmares or sleep disturbance, changed appetite, laughing or crying for no good reason, withdrawing from colleagues and family. Most paramedics never experience it — but recognizing it early is on you.
points.zh: PTSD 正是 CISD 想要预防的东西：一次格外惨烈的出勤，能让心理素质再好的救护员魂不守舍数周甚至数月。出现以下征象要向上级报告：事件在脑中挥之不去、闪回、噩梦或睡眠紊乱、食欲改变、无缘无故大笑或流泪、疏远同事与家人。大多数救护员一生不会经历 PTSD——但尽早识别它的责任在你自己。

points.en: Perspective points the chapter offers on resuscitation and mortality: for a resuscitation to succeed, everything has to go just right, and even across a long career you will not see many successful ones — 'losing' a patient stops being an identity wound once your ego is in check and the work is a calling. Attending births and deaths is framed as an honour: a private, in many cultures holy, moment you are invited into.
points.zh: 教材为复苏与死亡提供的心理定位：复苏要成功，每个环节都得恰好顺利，哪怕干满整个职业生涯，成功的复苏也不会多——当你管住自我、把这行当作使命，『没救回来』就很少再成为心结。见证出生与死亡被定义为一种荣幸：那是别人一生中最私密、在许多文化里神圣的时刻，而你是被邀请在场的人。

points.en: The chapter's driving creed: a paramedic's FIRST job is to come home safe to loved ones. Careers of 20 or 30 years without a single ambulance collision are not luck — safety is deliberate, operating an ambulance is a public trust, and driving one is always dangerous. The ambulance itself is a four-sided billboard broadcasting your respect, courtesy, and concern — or the lack of all three.
points.zh: 本章的驾驶信条：救护员的第一要务是平安回家见到亲人。干满二三十年零事故的救护员不是运气好——安全是刻意经营出来的，开救护车是一份公共信任，而且开救护车永远是危险的。救护车本身就是块四面广告牌，时刻向公众播报你的尊重、礼让与体恤——或三样全无。

points.en: The proven safety tips, each testable: warning equipment ASKS for right of way, never demands it; always allow for other drivers' incompetence; come to a full complete stop at an opposing signal and proceed only after others can anticipate your intentions; when a driver panics, kill the siren, switch to the PA, and politely repeat 'Please pull to the right and stop'; at freeway speed drivers may not hear the siren — hang back far enough to appear in their mirrors and expect them to slam the brakes when they finally notice; and when someone refuses to yield, control your emotions instead of reacting.
points.zh: 教材背书的驾驶安全法则，条条可考：警示装置是用来『请求』路权的，绝不是索要；永远为其他司机的失误预留余地；遇对向信号灯要完全停稳，等别人有时间、有依据预判你的意图后再走；对方司机慌了神，就关掉警笛、切到车外广播，礼貌地说『请靠右停车，谢谢』，听不懂就再说一遍；高速路况下别人未必听得到警笛——保持足够车距让警灯出现在对方后视镜里，并预判他们发现你后的第一反应是猛踩刹车；遇到拒不让行的，管住情绪、别针锋相对。

points.en: Lights-and-siren transport needs a justification you can document: can the risk to you, the patient, and the public be justified to save a few minutes — and will those minutes actually change the patient's outcome? If you transported emergently, the record must show why.
points.zh: 开警灯警笛转运需要一个能写进文书的理由：为省这几分钟，让你、患者和公众承担的风险说得过去吗？省下的几分钟真会改变患者的结局吗？只要你选择了紧急转运，记录里就必须写清依据。

points.en: Escorts are a trap: the average driver hears one siren and sees only the first vehicle of a convoy in the mirror — deliberately running an escort is called both pompous and dangerous. Minimize warning-equipment use and the number of vehicles per response. In bad weather — fog, blowing snow, slick asphalt — expect the worst decisions from every driver including yourself: slow down, and book emergency driving classes before the bad season arrives.
points.zh: 护送车队是个坑：普通司机只听得见一声警笛、后视镜里只看得见车队的第一辆车——刻意组织护送被教材评为既自大又危险。要尽量减少警示装置的使用次数和单次出勤的车辆数。恶劣天气——雾、风雪、湿滑路面——要预设每个司机（包括你自己）都会做出最糟的决定：放慢车速，并赶在坏天气季节来临前就报名紧急驾驶课程。

points.en: Parking doctrine flipped by one fact: ambulances load from the REAR. The old teaching — shield with the vehicle, front wheels turned into traffic — suits police needing headlamp illumination or fire crews with front outlets, but not you. Protect your back; park in the best position for loading. Exception: if the ambulance is first on scene it takes the protective position — knowing it must be moved later.
points.zh: 一条事实颠覆了停车教条：救护车从『车尾』装载患者。老教法——用车身作掩护、前轮打向车流——适合需要大灯照明的警察或有前置出水口的消防，唯独不适合你。护住你的车尾，把车停在最利于装载的位置。例外：救护车是第一辆到场的车辆时，先承担掩护位——但心里记着它稍后必须挪走。

points.en: Due regard is grounded in ownership: your certificate, equipment, radio frequencies, roads — and the occasional prerogative to override certain traffic laws — all belong to the public. Those who abused the privilege report a horror no teacher can describe after causing a fatality, traceable to something that took a couple of seconds; there is no undo button. And the chapter's closing aphorism: speed is sometimes perceived as the essence of EMS, but knowledge is the essence of the professional paramedic.
points.zh: 『应尽注意』（due regard）的根基是产权：你的证书、装备、无线电频段、道路——连同偶尔可豁免部分交规的特权——统统属于公众。滥用过这份特权的人说，酿成死亡事故（尤其死的是同行）之后那个早晨的恐惧，没有任何老师能形容；而起因往往只是短短两秒的事，驾驶没有撤销键。本章收尾格言：速度常被当作 EMS 的精髓，但知识才是职业救护员的精髓。

sections.titleEn: Protecting Yourself: Infection Control, Hostile Scenes, Traffic
sections.titleZh: 自我防护：感染控制、敌意现场与道路现场

points.en: Minimum PPE every ambulance must carry: gloves, facial protection (masks and eyewear), gowns, and N95 respirators. The cultural note that frames it: getting messy on shift was once a status symbol — like the proudly filthy surgical aprons of the 1800s that spread disease by the score; the modern paramedic's pride is endangering no one, patient included.
points.zh: 每辆救护车必备的最低 PPE 配置：手套、面部防护（口罩与护目镜）、隔离衣、N95 呼吸器。教材给的文化注脚：曾几何时，一身脏污是『扛造』的勋章——就像19世纪外科医生引以为傲的脏手术围裙，实则成打地传播疾病；现代救护员的骄傲是不让任何人暴露于危险，包括患者。

points.en: Glove discipline beyond 'wear them': some encounters need more than one set — don a fresh pair after intubating or starting an IV, before loading the patient; wear gloves to sanitize the ambulance or even to handle cleaning rags; reserve the pricier sterile gloves for clean or sterile procedures; and whatever you were doing — take the gloves OFF before you drive.
points.zh: 手套纪律不止『戴上』：一次接触可能要换好几副——插管或开静脉之后、装载患者之前，换上新手套；给救护车消毒、甚至碰清洁抹布也要戴手套；更贵的无菌手套只留给清洁/无菌操作用；还有——无论刚才在干什么，开车之前必须把手套摘掉。

points.en: The handwashing standard: wash vigorously with antibacterial soap for at least 30 seconds before rinsing; no soap and water, use waterless wipes — their active ingredient, isopropyl alcohol, is a very effective bactericide. When to wash: before and after the bathroom, before ingesting anything, before getting into your personal car, and before and after any contact with a patient or instrument — busy caseloads once meant more than 30 washes a day. Every infection-control text starts and ends with the same order: wash your hands.
points.zh: 洗手标准：用抗菌皂用力搓洗至少30秒再冲净；没有皂和水就用免水清洁湿巾——其有效成分异丙醇是高效杀菌剂。何时洗：如厕前后、任何东西入口前、上自己私家车前、接触患者或器械前后——出勤繁忙时一天洗手30多次并不稀奇。所有感染控制教科书都以同一句话开头和收尾：把手洗了。

points.en: The forgotten barrier maintenance: hand lotion several times a day, on and off duty — intact skin is a highly effective pathogen barrier, but frequent washing dries and cracks it, breaching your own armour. Eye protection: antisplash eyewear through any patient contact is good practice, an absolute necessity during suctioning and intubation — where a full face shield may serve better.
points.zh: 最易被忘记的屏障保养：每天多次涂护手霜，当班休班都要——完整的皮肤是极有效的病原体屏障，但频繁洗手会把它洗干、洗裂，等于自毁盔甲。眼部防护：任何患者接触全程戴防溅护目镜是好习惯，吸引和插管操作时则是绝对必需——插管时干脆用全面部防护屏更稳妥。

points.en: Respiratory rules with their numbers: have a cold, wear a mask — protecting others from you and you from a second infection while weakened; bad cold, active cough, or fever — stay home. Many Canadian jurisdictions mandate influenza immunization for health care workers, because influenza causes tens of thousands of hospitalizations and thousands of deaths each year in Canada. For tuberculosis — an estimated 1.7 billion people affected worldwide and 3 million deaths a year — the surgical mask is not enough: wear the N95 respirator.
points.zh: 呼吸道规则连着它的数字：感冒了就戴口罩——既保护别人不被你传染，也保护虚弱期的你不再中招；重感冒、活动性咳嗽或发热——直接留在家里。加拿大许多辖区已对医护人员强制流感疫苗接种，因为流感每年在加拿大造成数万人住院、数千人死亡。至于结核——全球估计17亿人受累、每年300万人死亡——普通外科口罩不够格：必须戴 N95 呼吸器。

points.en: Cleaning schedule with teeth: patient-compartment surfaces (stretcher, bench seat, grab rails, deck, door-handle areas) plus cab hardware, steering wheel, and gearshift — daily AND after every call; stretcher mounts come off at least once a week to clear accumulated dried blood and vomit that breeds odour and flies; pen sanitized or replaced often; stethoscope wiped with alcohol after every call. The decontamination ladder: single-use items are discarded into hazmat bags; equipment that touched intact skin gets a commercial disinfectant or 1:10 diluted bleach; anything that entered the body's interior — a laryngoscope blade — must be sterilized with chemical agents or pressurized steam, because only sterilization kills ALL microorganisms.
points.zh: 有硬性周期的清洁表：患者舱表面（担架、长椅、扶手、地板、门把手区域）加驾驶室五金、方向盘、换挡杆——每天清洁且每单出勤后再清洁一次；担架固定座至少每周拆下一次，清除积攒的干涸血迹与呕吐物——那是臭味与苍蝇之源；笔要常消毒或换新；听诊器每单出勤后用酒精擦拭。去污阶梯：一次性用品直接投入危险品袋；接触过完整皮肤的器械用商用消毒剂或1:10稀释漂白水消毒；进入过人体内部的器械——如喉镜片——必须用化学灭菌剂或高压蒸汽灭菌，因为只有灭菌能杀灭全部微生物。

points.en: Exposure management runs five steps: soap-and-water washing of the exposed area right away; meeting every reporting requirement; a medical evaluation; the appropriate booster immunizations; and a written record of the incident that names what was done to cut the infection risk. Sharps go only into dedicated containers — a large one on the ambulance, a small one in the carry-in gear.
points.zh: 职业暴露处置五步：立即用肥皂和水清洗暴露部位；履行全部上报要求；接受医学评估；补齐相应的疫苗加强针；记录事件全程——包括你为降低感染风险采取了哪些措施。锐器只进专用容器——车上放大号，随身包里配小号。

points.en: Hostile-scene doctrine: when hostility is known or anticipated, EMS and first responders should never arrive first — a December 2003 NAEMSP position statement first formally endorsed prehospital caregivers' own right to safety, and modern jurisdictions have paramedics stand back until police defuse the scene. The suspicious dispatch list warranting initial police response: fight, stabbing, shooting, domestic disturbance, 'person down', and 'unknown medical aid' — and the most worrisome calls of all carry limited or vague caller information, because a caller withholding details may be hiding something. Asking police to go in first does not make you less of a caregiver: you cannot treat anyone if you are hurt.
points.zh: 敌意现场信条：凡是已知或可预见敌意的现场，EMS 和第一响应者绝不能最先到场——2003年12月 NAEMSP 的立场声明首次正式确认院前救护者自身的安全权利，现代辖区普遍要求救护员退后等警方控制局面。需要警察先行进入的可疑派遣类型：斗殴、捅刺、枪击、家庭纠纷、『有人倒地』、『不明医疗求助』——而最令人担忧的，是报警人信息稀少含糊的呼叫：不肯向调度透露细节的人，可能正有事要藏。请警察先进门丝毫不损你作为救护者的成色：你若受伤，谁也救不了。

points.en: Managing the hostile patient: listen far more than you talk, never argue, and work on de-escalation — upset people neither listen nor reason well (fight-or-flight again), and many willing patients turned unwilling because a crew member could not resist a witty comment. Verbal judo is the named discipline: like the soft martial art, it deflects energy rather than inflicting it. Terrain warning: on someone else's turf they hold every advantage — they know the environment and the weapon locations, you know nothing, and volatile patients are most dangerous in their own homes, especially in poor lighting. Trust your intuition (the book assigns De Becker's The Gift of Fear): it processes small details your rational mind discounts.
points.zh: 对付敌意患者：多听少说、绝不抬杠、专注降温——情绪激动的人既听不进也想不通（又是战或逃反应），而许多本来愿意去医院的患者，就因为哪个队员没忍住抖机灵而变卦。教材点名的功夫叫『言语柔道』：如同柔道这门以柔克刚的武术，它化解力道而不是施加力道。地形警告：在别人的地盘上，优势全在对方——环境和武器藏在哪他一清二楚，你一无所知；易爆患者在自己家里最危险，光线昏暗时尤甚。相信直觉（教材指定阅读 De Becker 的《恐惧的礼物》）：直觉处理的是被理性折扣掉的微小细节。

points.en: Traffic scenes kill the comfortable: the most dangerous calls are the everyday ones, precisely because familiarity breeds complacency. Put on the high-visibility vest or jacket BEFORE exiting the ambulance. Begin physical observations about 1.5 km out — traffic, wind direction, smoke, approaching darkness, weather — and as first unit on scene, assess and radio actual or potential hazards to incoming units. Vehicle-generated hazards to anticipate: an undercarriage hot from even a 5-to-10-minute drive can ignite dry grass or a liquid spill you park over; fuel dripping onto hot exhaust or electrical arcing can start fire mid-scene; and your own scattered equipment packaging becomes a trip hazard. Early on, traffic control can matter more than medicine.
points.zh: 道路现场专杀『熟练工』：最危险的正是天天跑的普通呼叫，因为熟悉滋生松懈。高可见度反光背心或外套要在下车**之前**穿好。距现场约1.5公里就开始观察——车流、风向、烟雾、天色渐暗与天气变化——作为首车到场，先做现场评估并把现存和潜在危险通报给后续单位。要预判车辆自身制造的危险：哪怕只开了5到10分钟，底盘也已滚烫，停在干草或液体泄漏物上就是引火；燃油滴上灼热排气管、电线打火，都能让现场中途起火；自己乱扔的设备包装还会变成绊倒陷阱。在最初阶段，交通管制可能比医疗更重要。

points.en: The running case study lands two verdicts worth carrying: lifting a patient of very large size takes no fewer than four responders — call for resources whenever ambulances, supplies, equipment, or personnel feel inadequate; and probation pressure never outranks safety: speaking up about an unsafe lift is your responsibility even when it makes things awkward with a partner, because staying agreeable cost the narrator an injury, the partner an injury, a patient a fall, and the department its image.
points.zh: 贯穿全章的案例敲定两条结论：抬超大体型患者不得少于四名人员——只要觉得车辆、耗材、装备或人手不够，就呼叫增援；试用期的压力永远排在安全后面：对不安全的抬举开口叫停是你的责任，哪怕会让搭档脸上挂不住——案例里那位选择随和沉默的新人，最终搭进去的是自己的腰、搭档的伤、摔落的患者和整个部门的声誉。

atScene.en: Recruit your coworkers into a shared health-maintenance plan covering nutrition, exercise, and mental health — it prolongs careers and builds teamwork at the same time.
atScene.zh: 把同事拉进一套覆盖营养、运动、心理健康的共同健康计划——既延长职业寿命，又顺手炼出团队默契。

atScene.en: Learn to scan colleagues and patients for signs of stress: early discovery often prevents the situation from worsening.
atScene.zh: 练就扫描同事和患者压力征象的眼力：越早发现，越能阻止局面恶化。

atScene.en: Never assume a 'nonemergency' complaint means nothing is wrong — tunnel vision is a named cause of assessment mistakes and bad outcomes.
atScene.zh: 永远别默认『非紧急』主诉就没事——隧道视野被点名为评估失误和不良结局的根源之一。

atScene.en: First unit on any scene: do the scene assessment, radio actual and potential hazards to every responding unit — and remember your first job is the safety of the EMS crew, yourself included.
atScene.zh: 首车到达任何现场：先做现场评估，把现存与潜在危险用电台通报给所有后续单位——并记住你的第一职责是 EMS 班组的安全，包括你自己。

atScene.en: Every advanced infection-control text opens and closes with the same order — wash your hands: 30-plus seconds of vigorous scrubbing with antibacterial soap, or isopropyl-alcohol wipes when there is no water.
atScene.zh: 所有进阶感染控制教材的第一句和最后一句都是同一道命令——洗手：抗菌皂用力搓洗30秒以上，没水就用异丙醇免洗湿巾。

confusions.en: Eustress versus distress: both are Selye's stress, but eustress motivates achievement while distress overwhelms and debilitates. 'All stress must be avoided' is wrong twice — stress drives adaptation and self-preservation, and mild stress sharpens mental acuity.
confusions.zh: Eustress 与 distress 之辨：都是 Selye 定义下的压力，但前者推动成就，后者压垮心智。『压力都该避免』错了两次——压力驱动适应与自保，而且轻度压力反而让头脑更锐利。

confusions.en: Defusing versus formal debriefing: the defusing is about 30 minutes, held immediately after the call, to bleed off explosive pressure; the formal CISD is run by professional counsellors 24 to 72 hours later, lasts about 3 hours, off-site and confidential. Swapping the timings is the classic exam error.
confusions.zh: Defusing 与正式 debriefing 之辨：defusing 约30分钟、紧接出勤之后，为的是先把『炸药』泄压；正式 CISD 由专业辅导员在24–72小时后主持，约3小时，异地且保密。把两者的时间参数互换是最经典的考试错法。

confusions.en: Disinfection versus sterilization: a commercial disinfectant or 1:10 bleach kills MANY organisms and suffices for equipment that touched intact skin; only sterilization — chemical sterilant or pressurized steam — kills ALL microorganisms, and it is mandatory for anything that entered the body's interior, like a laryngoscope blade.
confusions.zh: 消毒与灭菌之辨：商用消毒剂或1:10漂白水杀灭『多数』微生物，对只接触过完整皮肤的器械足够；只有灭菌——化学灭菌剂或高压蒸汽——才能杀灭『全部』微生物，凡进入过人体内部的器械（如喉镜片）必须灭菌。

confusions.en: 'Cheer up the grieving.' In the depression stage of Kübler-Ross's model this is exactly wrong: the person wants permission to express sorrow — words, tears, or the silence beyond words — not distraction from it. Steer behaviour only when it is harmful.
confusions.zh: 『安慰一下，让他开心起来。』——在 Kübler-Ross 模型的抑郁期，这恰恰做反了：对方要的是获准表达悲伤——语言、眼泪、或超越言语的沉默——而不是被岔开。只有行为有害时才需要引导。

confusions.en: 'Shield the family from the body, and say he passed away gently.' Both instincts backfire: families blocked from seeing the body can be locked in denial and unable to grieve, and euphemisms deny them the word they need to hear — 'dead'. Hide the body from the public, never from the family.
confusions.zh: 『别让家属看到遗体，就说他安详地走了。』——两个本能都帮倒忙：见不到遗体的家属可能被锁死在否认里、迈不进哀伤程序，而委婉语剥夺了他们必须听到的那个词——『死亡』。遗体要对公众遮挡，绝不对家属遮挡。

confusions.en: 'The angry patient is angry at me.' Displacement says otherwise: the emotion belongs to the illness, the fate, the self — you are merely the nearest target. The professional caregiver accepts it without complaint; taking it personally is how crews escalate scenes.
confusions.zh: 『这个患者在冲我发火。』——转移机制说：不是。那份情绪属于疾病、命运或他自己——你只是离得最近的靶子。专业救护者照单全收、不去计较；把它当成针对个人，正是把现场越搞越僵的起点。

confusions.en: 'Angle the front wheels into traffic and shield the scene with the vehicle.' That doctrine belongs to police and fire. Ambulances load from the REAR — park to protect your back and optimize loading, taking the shielding position only when you are first on scene, and expecting to move later.
confusions.zh: 『前轮打向车流、用车身掩护现场。』——那是警车和消防车的教条。救护车从车尾装载——停车要护住车尾、以装载为先，只有首车到场时才先占掩护位，并且明白稍后得挪车。

mnemonics.name: 哀伤五阶 DABDA
mnemonics.en: Kübler-Ross in order: Denial, Anger, Bargaining, Depression, Acceptance — DABDA. Each stage is an adaptation, not a malfunction.
mnemonics.zh: Kübler-Ross 顺序：否认（D）、愤怒（A）、讨价还价（B）、抑郁（D）、接受（A）——DABDA。中文串：『否怒价抑受』。每一阶都是适应，不是故障。

mnemonics.name: 暴露五步：洗报评补记
mnemonics.en: After a blood or body-fluid exposure: Wash, Report, get Evaluated, Boost immunizations, Document.
mnemonics.zh: 血液/体液暴露后五步：洗（立即皂水清洗）→ 报（履行上报）→ 评（医学评估）→ 补（补种加强针）→ 记（记录事件与措施）。

mnemonics.name: 现场自控三招
mnemonics.en: Breathe (nose in, mouth out), Reframe ('I trust my training'), Relax progressively (tense-release after the call) — the three named stress tools, in order of when you use them.
mnemonics.zh: 控呼吸（鼻吸口呼）→ 重构（『我相信我的训练』）→ 渐进放松（收队后逐组绷紧-放松）——三种点名减压技术，按使用时机排好。

mnemonics.name: MCI 五反应
mnemonics.en: Anxiety (give a task), Blind panic (isolate fast — it spreads), Depression (bring back, remove), Overreaction (out of the treatment area), Conversion hysteria (anxiety turned into blindness, deafness, paralysis).
mnemonics.zh: 群伤现场五反应连处置：焦虑（派个任务）、盲目恐慌（火速隔离——会传染）、抑郁（唤回现实、带离）、过度反应（请出救治区）、转换性癔症（焦虑变失明/失聪/瘫痪）。

selfCheck.qEn: Calculate the target heart rate for a 40-year-old with a resting heart rate of 70, showing the formula.
selfCheck.qZh: 用公式算出一名 40 岁、静息心率 70 的人的目标心率。
selfCheck.aEn: Maximum HR = 220 − 40 = 180. (180 − 70) × 0.7 = 77. Target = 77 + 70 = 147 beats/min — roughly 70% of maximum, held for part of the workout without overexertion.

selfCheck.qEn: Name Kübler-Ross's five stages in order, and state the caregiver's correct behaviour in the depression stage.
selfCheck.qZh: 按顺序说出 Kübler-Ross 五阶段，并说明抑郁期照护者的正确做法。
selfCheck.aEn: Denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance. In depression: do not cheer them up — acknowledge the loss, offer tissues or a hug if wanted, accommodate a wish for quiet, and only redirect behaviour that is harmful.
selfCheck.aZh: 否认、愤怒、讨价还价、抑郁、接受。抑郁期：不要哄人开心——承认其失去、想哭递纸巾、想抱就抱、想独处就配合，只有行为有害时才干预。

selfCheck.qEn: Defusing versus formal CISD: give the timing and duration of each, and the evidence caveat the book attaches.
selfCheck.qZh: Defusing 与正式 CISD：各自的时机与时长？教材附带的证据保留是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Defusing: about 30 minutes, immediately after the call. Formal CISD: coordinated by professional counsellors 24 to 72 hours post-incident, about 3 hours, away from the workplace, confidential. Caveat: after more than 20 years of use there is no evidence CISDs are effective, nor that their effects are not harmful — and debriefings are offered, never forced.
selfCheck.aZh: Defusing：约30分钟，出勤后立即进行。正式 CISD：由专业辅导员在事后24–72小时组织，约3小时，异地保密。保留意见：使用20多年仍无有效性证据，也无『无害』的证据——且复盘只能提供、绝不强制。

selfCheck.qEn: A laryngoscope blade and a blood pressure cuff both need cleaning after a call. What does each require, and why are they different?
selfCheck.qZh: 一支喉镜片和一个血压袖带出勤后都要清洁，各需要什么处理？为什么不同？
selfCheck.aEn: The cuff touched intact skin: a commercial disinfectant or 1:10 diluted bleach suffices — disinfection kills many organisms. The blade entered the body's interior: it must be sterilized with a chemical sterilant or pressurized steam, because only sterilization kills all microorganisms.
selfCheck.aZh: 袖带只接触完整皮肤：商用消毒剂或1:10漂白水即可——消毒杀灭多数微生物。喉镜片进入过人体内部：必须以化学灭菌剂或高压蒸汽灭菌——只有灭菌能杀灭全部微生物。

selfCheck.qEn: You are splashed with a patient's blood. Walk through the five management steps.
selfCheck.qZh: 你被患者血液溅到，说出处置的五个步骤。
selfCheck.aEn: Immediate soap-and-water washing of the exposed site; then report it per your service's requirements; undergo medical evaluation; receive any needed immunization boosters; and finish with full documentation, naming the risk-reduction actions you took.
selfCheck.aZh: 立即用肥皂和水清洗暴露部位；履行全部上报要求；接受医学评估；补齐相应免疫加强针；记录事件全程，包括为降低感染风险采取的措施。

selfCheck.qEn: Which dispatch types does the book say are suspicious enough to warrant police arriving first?
selfCheck.qZh: 教材点名哪几类派遣性质可疑到需要警察先到场？
selfCheck.aEn: Fight, stabbing, shooting, domestic disturbance, 'person down', and 'unknown medical aid' — plus any call your intuition flags as violent, and especially calls with limited or vague caller information.
selfCheck.aZh: 斗殴、捅刺、枪击、家庭纠纷、『有人倒地』、『不明医疗求助』——外加任何被你的直觉标记为暴力的呼叫，尤其是报警人信息稀少含糊的那种。

selfCheck.qEn: List the impending-burnout warning signs you can recite — the book names eleven.
selfCheck.qZh: 背出你记得的倦怠先兆——教材列了十一项。
selfCheck.aEn: Chronic fatigue and irritability; cynical negative attitudes; no desire to report to work; emotional instability; changed sleep with unrefreshing waking; feeling overwhelmed, helpless, or hopeless; lost interest in hobbies; decreased concentration; declining health (colds, stomach upsets, headaches, backaches); constant muscle tightness; overeating, smoking, or drug/alcohol abuse.
selfCheck.aZh: 慢性疲劳与易怒；犬儒式消极；不想上班；情绪不稳；睡眠改变且醒来不解乏；被压垮/无助/无望感；对爱好失去兴趣；专注力下降；健康走低（感冒、胃部不适、头痛背痛）；肌肉持续紧绷；暴食、吸烟或药物酒精滥用。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Scene assessment + PPE is a scored block on every BC practical station
bcAlerts.topicZh: 现场评估＋PPE 在 BC 实操每一站都是计分板块
bcAlerts.bookEn: The textbook teaches routine precautions and scene awareness as professional habits, without attaching marks to them.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材把常规预防与现场警觉当作职业习惯来教，并不与分数挂钩。
bcAlerts.bcEn: On the EMALB practical exam, Scene Assessment and PPE form an explicit deduction block (5%/3%/1% tiers). The SA components to verbalize before touching the patient: hazards, environment, MOI, and number of patients. PPE means gloves, goggles, and mask; failing to verbalize the full SA first, ignoring a clearly presented hazard, or donning NO needed PPE costs the full 5%. Details: glasses wearers still don safety goggles unless their own meet the industry standard, and N95 is required — and may be verbalized — only when the patient presentation indicates it.
bcAlerts.bcZh: EMALB 实操考试把『现场评估＋PPE』设为明确的扣分板块（5%/3%/1% 三档）。开始接触患者前必须口述完整 SA 四要素：危险因素、环境、受伤机制（MOI）、患者人数。PPE 指手套、护目镜、口罩；未先口述完整 SA、对明摆着的危险视而不见、或需要时一件 PPE 都没戴，直接扣满 5%。细则：戴眼镜的考生除非自己的眼镜达到工业标准，否则仍须戴护目镜；N95 仅在患者表现有指征时才要求，且可以口述代替。

bcAlerts.bookEn: The book treats PTSD as a personal-recognition issue — know the signs, tell your superiors, use debriefing supports.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材把 PTSD 当作个人识别问题来处理——认识征象、报告上级、利用复盘支持。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC adds a legal backstop: since 2018 the Workers Compensation Act has carried a mental-disorder presumption for first responders, paramedics included — a diagnosed mental disorder such as PTSD is presumed work-related for WorkSafeBC claims, without the worker having to prove the causal link call by call.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 另有一层法律托底：自 2018 年起，《工伤保险法》为包括救护员在内的第一响应者设立心理障碍工伤推定——确诊的心理障碍（如 PTSD）在 WorkSafeBC 理赔中默认视为因工所致，无需伤者逐案自证因果。
